name: Horseshoe Kidney

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Horseshoe Kidney

criteria.description: Presence of fusion of the lower poles of both kidneys forming a U-shaped structure
Abnormal position of kidneys lower than usual in the abdomen
Imaging confirmation via ultrasound, CT, or MRI showing isthmus connecting kidneys
Evidence of urinary tract obstruction or hydronephrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of fusion of lower poles forming a U-shaped kidney with abnormal renal position
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiologic; clinical symptoms may be absent or nonspecific.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass corresponding to fused renal isthmus
pathognomonic.notes: May be detected during physical examination

common.symptomName: Flank pain due to obstruction or stones

occasional.notes: May develop secondary to renal impairment
Increased risk due to urinary stasis

rare.symptomName: Associated congenital anomalies (e.g., Turner syndrome, trisomy 18)

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine in advanced cases
Urine culture positive in urinary tract infections
imaging: Ultrasound showing fused lower poles and isthmus
CT or MRI confirming horseshoe shape and associated complications
Intravenous pyelogram demonstrating abnormal renal drainage
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; associated with chromosomal anomalies in syndromic cases
other: Physical exam may reveal palpable abdominal mass
Increased risk of obstruction and nephrolithiasis

distinguishingFeatures: Kidney located abnormally but not fused
Both kidneys located on same side of abdomen
Fusion present but different anatomical configuration

redFlags: Severe flank pain with signs of obstruction
Recurrent urinary tract infections unresponsive to treatment
references: Brenner BM. The Kidney. 9th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Sweeney DE, et al. Horseshoe kidney: clinical and radiologic features. Radiographics. 2018;38(3): 1021-1035.
